I just bought my first kcup coffee machine last month. I don't think coffee myself and my hubby only likes a cup here and there. It never seemed worth making a whole pot of coffee. So I thought this would be the way to go. A quick and easy cup of coffee. Unfortunately, I hadn't planned on it being so easy that he wanted more coffee than normal.  Then the $$$ started adding up quickly on the purchases of kcups.  I was looking at the replacement kcups and was not thrilled with having to remove the holder that pierces the normal kcups and put in the replacement holder. How often would I have to change back and forth between my coffee and the kcup holder. Then I saw the simple cups.  I watched a video on another review and thought why not give it a shot. I am so glad that I did. It was very easy to do. Put the cup in the holder, add the filter, add the coffee , and put on the lid. Putting on the lid is quite easy with the holder/stand.  There you have your own kcups.  I did notice that strength was not quite as strong as the regular kcups. This is not a problem for us. I always have to add more water to the cup after the brewing was done on a regular kcup.  There is a  little water that stays on top of the cup due to the design of the lid. It is very little. I was able to reuse the cup (not the filter).  I just lined up the holes with the piercers in the machine. He is happy to get more coffee. I am happy to be able to use our own coffee.

Received this a a gift.  I prepared the simple cup per directions, placed in the Keurig and began brew. Only about a third of the water went through the cup. Upon inspection I found that the cup filter splits open and the coffee grounds collect in the bottom of the simple cup and clog the drip line. The coffee that did make it to the cup is full of grounds. I tried three time to make a cup of coffee' 1st time filing the filter to 90% capacity, 2nd time to 75% capacity, and the 3rd time filled to 50% capacity. Each brew time I only received about 2 ounces of coffee ground filled coffee. I opened each simple cup and inspected the filters and each one had split in one or more places thus allowing the coffee grounds to clog the machine. Not only did I waste 3 simple cups and filters but also equivalent amount of coffee and 6 teaspoons of sugar. Additionally, I had to dismantle and clean the Keurig receptacle.

Fit perfectly and my washing machine no longer leaks. If your machine is leaking from the very bottom of the seal, like mine was, you may want to do the following. First check for any holes or tears in the rubber. If you cannot find any then remove the outer spring clamp and tighten the inner band clamp before removing any panels.  If the adjusting screw on the inner band clamp is perpendicular to the band, like mine is, you can tighten it with a socket and extension. I wish I would have done this before ordering a new seal since my band clamp was very loose and thus the reason it was leaking.

This was really easy to install. Watch the youtube videos to see how. Be careful, and pay attention to its orientation. Those who have complained about it tearing easily may have installed it improperly. It goes on in a specific orientation (there is a drain hole) and must not be twisted or it will be too tight and tear. Just a little caution when clamping it down and you will be fine.

I've had this installed for 6 months and it is working perfectly. Don't pay a service guy to change this. If you are reasonable good with tools and have a reasonable attention to detail (i.e. getting it on straight), then you should be able to do this.

I was surprised when I used the brush how much lint was in the vent. The brush does a good job of holding onto the lint and pushing the clogs through. Though you have to push a little harder, the rods are flexible enough to work through bends/curves in the duct.

The 12' kit was not enough to go from one side of the duct to the other (I wish that they sold a 6' extension rather than just another 12'), and you want to avoid coming up short and creating a clog. You might want to play it safe and just get the extension kit from the start. Or, if one end of the duct is higher than the other (my outside vent is above my head, while the inside of the dryer duct is ground level), start from the high end and push through to let the lint fall down the last bit of the duct.

The directions encourage you to tape the rods together before placing them in the duct. Though the rods easily twist into each other, the connection is not tight enough to prevent them from coming apart if you accidentally turn counter-clockwise, so the duck tape is necessary. The brush works very well, and if the rods were longer and held together without duck tape, I'd give five stars. Even with needing some duck tape and maybe needed to purchase the extension kit, this brush is much cheaper than having someone clean the dryer duct for you and much cheaper than other home versions available online and in stores.

Note: be aware of what direction your drill is spinning. If your drill is spinning counter clock wise you may inadvertently loosen the extension rods from each other thus leaving the brush stuck several feet down the pipe (whoops). This is not a design flaw just the nature of tightening and loosening.

Initially, there was a really nasty smell (like something crawled up there and died) - after the duct cleaner came out the first time he didn't find anything but got a lot of lint out and sprayed bleach inside. While the really awful smell was now mostly gone, not long after, the mildew smell became pretty noticeable. I don't think the brush the duct cleaning company had was long enough to reach in to get to the trouble spots. He was running a blower and got a lot of lint out but the smell persisted even after he came out a second time and sprayed bleach into the duct with a compressed air gun.

At this point I decided to DIY it, and I'm glad I did. This review is more detailed than most of my reviews for the simple fact that there is a lot of confusion on how this ice maker works. I love this icemaker. 9 donuts are made every 6-8 minutes depending on selected size. Two sizes are available--Small or large. Simply fill the reserve up with water and press "start"! You will have ice in as little as 6 minutes! The basket will hold quite a bit. Once the basket is full, a sensor is triggered and it does stop producing until either you empty the basket or the ice melts back into the reserve. I feel it is important to mention that there is no "freezer" to keep the ice cubes frozen and if the ice sets a bit it will melt back into the reserve to be reused but the ice stays frozen for awhile. I have noticed several complaints when dumping into your ice bucket in the freezer, the ice will freeze together due to it being a "wet" (but solid) ice. Simply take a knife and break it up after each time you dump in the freezer and it's fine.

The new version does not include an integrated O-ring and the guide threads are not continuous, but have a gap between the start point and the endpoint of the threads. This results in less friction needed to keep the water filter in place. Also the two small tabs in the inside top of the water filter that depress the switch which allows water to flow into the filter must be of a different size or in a different position. The new version does not depress the switch far enough to cause water to flow. Suggest purchasing the original GE version or, if you have good water in your area, purchase the filter bypass cap appropriate for your refrigerator.

This is NOT an "NSF 53" filter! It is an "NSF 42" filter.

You should note that there are two main levels of filtration, one for taste & odor ("NSF 42") and the other for health and contaminants ("NSF 53"). This filter is the LOWER level filter which may be fine for you but just be aware that this is why it is cheaper than some other OEM filters. If you want to eliminate toxins then get the higher filtration level NSF 53.

NSF 42 filters out: Chlorine
NSF 53 filters out: Chlorine, asbestos, Cyst., Atrazine, Benzine, Lindane, Carbofuran, D-Dichlorbenzene, Lead, Mercury, and other "Particulate class 1" elements.

Also note that this filter is “Tested to NSF Standards” vs NSF Certified, Know the difference. Some products are NSF certified. Some only claim to be “tested to NSF Standards.” What’s the difference? One is actually tested and the other is a marketing claim that is not certified.

First batch of 9 cubes came in less than 5 minutes, and they kept coming until the basket was full. Water gets pumped up into a mini reservoir and forms around cold metal "fingers". When the ice is done, the water is drained back, the fingers heat briefly so the ice falls off, and the ice gets dumped in the basket for use.

My GE Hotpoint model no: HSS25IFMD WW fridge has gone out several times. The first time, it was the main board.

It recently had a defrost issue again. I assumed the problem was the same as before, so I made the mistake of replacing the main control board again prior to first replacing several smaller, inexpensive parts. The board and the heating element were replaced but did not fix the problem. Then I replaced the defrost thermostat and the freezer temperature sensor. I'm not exactly sure which one of these two fixed my defrost problem, but since they were both inexpensive, I replaced both. My fridge works perfectly again.

A couple things to keep in mind, you will need some wire strippers, wire nuts, and electrical tape to do these repairs correctly. Replacing this part is not time consuming or labor intensive at all. For installation instructions, search Youtube for installation videos.

***IMPORTANT***
Make sure you defrost the freezer coils before you expect this repair to take effect.

My defrost problem was as a result of my freezer not going into defrost mode as it should. After installing these new components, I expected the defrost cycle to start immediately, which would have been evident by seeing the defrost heater come on. This did not happen which made me sick, because I thought my repair was a failure. It was not until I defrosted the freezer coils and started the freezer again that I saw the freezer go into defrost

We have a 10 year old Whirlpool washer that would "not" spin at times. Because it would spin and work just fine sometimes I was thinking the problem was inside the transmission. I ordered a coupling, a clutch kit and the neutral drain kit. I figured if I had the transmission out and the problem was not the coupling or the clutch I wanted to proceed to rebuilding the transmission and have the parts on hand. After removing the pump, motor, and then the transmission I determined the coupling was good but I had a new one so I replaced it. I then determined the clutch was warn/bad/lose/slipping. I installed the 285785 clutch kit, all the parts fit perfectly. I reinstalled everything and ran the washer through 15 loads of wash so far, some heavy some light, it works like new. We had not noticed that it was spinning slower (when it did spin) and now with the new clutch the wash is drying much faster as more water is being removed.

I don't care for the "new" (HE) washers as on most you do not have the choices I have with my old one. Bottom line, instead of spending five to seven hundred dollars for a new washer I repaired my old one for under $35.00. The $20.00 dollar neutral spin kit I did not use I'll keep for now.

This is the third type of reusable k-cup coffee filter that I've tried, and frankly, it was going to be the last, since I've been less than impressed by the functioning of the others tried.  These, however, are the best attempt to date that I've added to my Keurig single brew 'custom' option.  Firstly, you get four of them, so if you want several cups of coffee, you don't have to worry about cleaning the last one out, just grab another one.  Secondly, there's only one part in all, since the lid is attached to the body of the coffee filter.  So, easy to keep track of.  Thirdly, they work pretty well.  the key is not to fill them more than 1/4" from the top of the basket, and they shouldn't pour their guts out all over the machine like some others do, putting grinds into your coffee and around the coffee maker's innards as well.  They work best in my low level Keurig machine if only brewing at the mid size, or 8 oz. size cup I believe it is.  Easy to clean out, they are the best design and manufactured product of this type available out there.  Trust me.

When I finish making coffee, I take the Aeropress over the trash can, unscrew the black plastic cap, and push the grinds into the trashcan. Can't do that so easily with the metal filter: instead you have to push it up until the filter is accessible and, trying not to scald yourself on boiling hot dregs, remove the filter. Then you have to shake/scrape off the grinds that inevitably cling to the filter. There are inevitably some left behind, which I then rinse into the sink, but rinsing grinds into the sink is a good way to rack up a plumber's bill, so that's not the best choice. Because of Whirlpool's 2 manufacturers, I did not risk ordering my filter online, but went to my local Lowes where they had BOTH Everydrop #5 filters from the 2 manufacturers! For my 2005 fridge, I needed the Kemflo design with the flat top with notches cut into it (as pictured above in the one pack photo & from abed's one star review photo labeled "old model" --you can see the notches cut into the right side). The other #5 design was rounded on top (no notches) and manufactured by Mexico 1 (and is pictured in abed's review labeled "new model"). It's pretty poor that Whirlpool has 2 designs listed under the same part number (Everydrop 5) & even if you order directly from Whirlpool they cannot tell you which design will ship! The Whirlpool rep said that older model fridges (8-10 years old) need the filter made for Whirlpool by Kemflo in Taiwan that is flat with the notches in it. So, look at your current filter to see what you need! Then you will at least know which manufacturer design you need. Hope this is helpful for others!

Soon after receiving this ice maker I installed it in my fridge. It made two batches of ice and froze up. I removed it and noticed that the outside plastic piece with all the fingers on it was bowed out and encased in ice. I thawed the icemaker and started comparing it to the original. I noticed that the finger nearest the water inlet housing was hung up underneath the housing. On the original icemaker, this finger was cut off so it couldn't get hung up. I called the supplier, told him what I found, and he sent me another one. In the mean time I decided to try to fix the first one. I cut off the finger nearest the water inlet housing so that it matched the original. I also put a bead of type 1 clear silicone adhesive under the outside plastic housing where it contacts the mold. This was to make sure it was securely bonded. After waiting a day for the adhesive to set up, I re-installed the icemaker. It started working fine. I waited a few days to make sure it wasn't going to fail again, then returned the second one they sent me unopened. The only problem I noticed was that about half of the ice cubes we're hollow. I have never seen that before but decided I could live with that. Everything was ok for about three weeks, then it froze up again. I called the supplier back and he sent me a third icemaker. I haven't installed it yet. I'm going to modify it like I did the first one and hope for the best. Maybe this one will be ok.

The one big thing I can't abide is a company that tries to trick consumers into thinking the product is something that it isn't. Starting with the Amazon listing, Refresh wants to appear to be the original Samsung product. "Samsung Aqua-Pure DA29-00003G Water Filter..." That's written to deceive us.

And later, in the Description "...activated carbon block filter which has received NSF42 approval." That, and all references to NSF "approval" on the refreshmywater.com website are flat-out lies. The WQA has certified the Refresh products to certain NSF/ANSI standards for material safety and structural integrity ONLY. Not removal of solids, cysts, chemicals just materials of construction. This product has no independent certification of removal of foreign materials from your drinking water.

But on the Refresh website, they use the NSF logo and they have a whole page that would have us believe that they have received "Our filters are 100% NSF Certifed." Whatever that means!

I bought a couple cheap 5 gal. paint buckets at the hardware store and use them--fill them up and let the items soak overnight (or at least for 4+ hours), then use this blue thing to bash the items a bit.  I would say I bash for less then a minute (I imagine I'm churning butter just so I don't give up), then pour out the dirty water, refill with clean water, bash it a bit more, pour out that water and dump the wet items into a very big (cheap) colander/strainer I set in the bathroom sink (all washing and rinsing are done in the bathtub so I can splash all I want).  I do sheets too or one sheet at a time, and towels (1 bath, 2 smaller hand towels).  I can't do a whole lot of clothes at once, pair of jeans, couple of t-shirts, couple of underwear--I do maybe 2 washing per week of only our clothing. I ordered this for my Kenmore gas range because everything on it was working fine except for the oven. Sometimes it would light, sometimes it wouldn't. Even when it did light, I would have to wait about 30 seconds for the gas to turn on and ignite. When I researched the problem, this part appeared to be the most likely culprit. If it doesn't reach a high enough temperature, the gas to the oven won't turn on. The old part would either take about 30 seconds to get hot enough, or it wouldn't get hot enough and prevented the oven from lighting.

Update: we've lived with this for about a year now and we live in the lightning capital of the U.S. There have been numerous strikes in the neighborhood, multiple power failures (twice/month minimum), and there have been zero problems with our smart fridge now that we have this thing protecting it. The previous refrigerator had failed multiple times in the past ten years. The negative reviews (especially the ones with misspellings) stating "not U.L." are truly mystifying. The packaging is very clearly listed UL. I think for the money spent it's been a very worthwhile "investment".

Original: I love how this "times out" when there is a power failure. It prevents the fridge from turning immediately back on when power is restored. This is a saving grace for those brief off/on cycles that seem to happen here more frequently than I'm accustomed to after having lived out west. Because we did not have one of these installed on our previous refrigerator, the electronics and compressor eventually failed from the (fairly frequent) lightning-caused electrical-surge/power-failure/power-restoration cycles. This device has proven to be a very inexpensive insurance for our new fridge.

Overall, this unit does the job of cooking food, but it has some issues. First, the starter only works about 1/2 the time. Not a big deal, since I keep an extention lighter near by. My unit came with the cast iron burner elements covered in gold spraypaint for some reason. They smoked and stank the first few times I tried to cook with the unit. I'm guessing the fumes are not at all good for you and probably not something you want billowing up around your food. The four spoke pan supports don't offer a lot of stability to your pots and pans, especially smaller ones, 8" or less. They tend to slip off because the spokes don't extend far enough toward the center. Five or six spokes, each an inch longer, would be a significant improvement. The inner and outer ring of each element has an airflow adjuster under the glass surface. In my experience, the knobs and air adjustments don't give enough control. Even on the lowest setting, the center element has a high flame that will burn the food in the center of the pot or pan unless I turn the pressure way down at the tank regulator. Forget about a low simmer unless you are willing to monkey with the primary regulator. This unit is also bigger than it looks in the photos. The given dimensions are accurate, though, so lay out a piece of cardboard or the equivalent to get a sense of the actual scale before you order it. In retrospect, I probably could have chosen a smaller/cheaper unit and been just as satisfied.

The switch assembly fit perfectly and worked fine.  It was not hard to change.  I watched a couple of uTube videos for advice on changing this switch and wiring harness.  You need to remove two screws in the back of the control housing to tilt the housing back to unhook and remove the connector. You do NOT have to remove the sheet metal wrapper from the washer base, you can push the tub sideways enough to allow access to the clips that hold the wiring and access the bottom switch mounting screw.  New screws are not included, so you must save and re-use the screws.  A stubby phillips screwdriver helps.  Turns out, our switch had been replaced once before by cutting the wires near the switch and splicing in the new switch with "wire nut" connectors, a bad idea. These switches must be a consistent problem for Whirlpool top loaders.  This switch assembly has been in use for a couple of weeks with no problem.  I diagnosed the problem by lifting and closing the lid while the washer was supposed to be spinning.  The switch was erratic.  An electrical tester showed the switch was closing.  I suspect the contacts were burned and would not carry the required current.  For the low cost of this switch, replace it if your washer works well otherwise but won't spin.

If you love to chew ice, then you will love this ice maker.  The ice is best right out of the holding basket, but I will say that a big draw-back is that the ice is wet when you take it out of the holding area which isn't a big deal if you are going to use it immediately, but it is if you are making a bunch of ice for future use, not so great.  You can't put wet ice in the freezer or it will freeze together in a big lump.  The big lump of ice will have to be broken apart with an ice pick which give you sharp edges on the ice and as an ice chewer....not desirable.  So what I have been doing is taking a smaller batch of ice and putting it in a freezer bag and then placing the bag in the freezer with the ice spread out in a single layer.  Later on when it's all frozen, I break up the ice in the bag, trying to keep the ice as "whole" as possible and transfer the ice to the ice holder in the freezer.  Yes, I know it's a bit involved, but it works.  I wouldn't want this ice maker to be my sole source of ice, but I do like the small size "cubes" it puts out for small batches of ice chewing pleasure!

This clip does work in fooling the Keurig 2.0 machines into thinking that every attempt to brew is a 2.0 compatible K-Cup. However, if you have a more advanced model like my K-550, it assumes that a Keurig K-Cup is always installed in the unit. That presents several problems in that is it always ready to Brew...Ignores the time clock settings and overrides your chance to simply get hot water from your Keurig system.
If all you want to do is brew standard K-Cup coffee it works great ! If you want the option to brew K-Carafes or simply to get hot water for your Ramen Noodles, or to check the time, it does not work very well\

This same company sells Keurig 2.0 compatible stickers which you attach to the K-cup to make them 2.0 compatible and the system will automatically revert back to it's normal configuration when you remove the K-Cup with the override sticker.

You will need ot evaluate which works best for you.

By the way....I only received 5 Clever Clips instead of the 6X displayed in the Amazon order.

Until it died, I overall liked this ice maker. Some other comments about it:
- It makes ice quickly, but can only hold a moderate amount (2.3 lbs?), which is fine if you are emptying it regularly, but filling a large bag or cooler would take constant emptying all day.
- The cubes come out frozen but melt as they sit in the collection basket and so are are cold but a bit "melty".overall. They're not nearly as cold or hard as the cubes from my freezer's icemaker.
- This means they melt and dilute your drinks quicker, if that matters to you. It also means if you put them in a freezer to refreeze them, them tend to stick together..
- The ice maker itself can be quite noisy at times. Not just the clatter of ice as it is dumped but occasional assorted whines, groans, wheezes and whirs as it makes the ice, sometimes load enough to be heard at the far end of my house from the ice maker.
- We like to use filtered water for the ice maker. The PUR 18-cup dispenser/filter matches the capacity of the ice maker and works well for us.

A lot bigger than I expected!  Was very happy with that.  Your instructions are very self explanatory.  Ice maker can yield 48 pounds plus a day if you keep refilling it.  There are 3 different ice cube sizes, and the ice is the round kind with the hole in the end.  Makes very soft, easy to crunch ice.  The soft ice is my absolute favorite and that's what this makes.  Be sure that when you first get your ice maker you wait at least 30 minutes to plug it in, as it needs to settle in case it was turned upside down or shaken during delivery.  You are going to want to wipe down the inside really good with some vinegar to get the "new plastic" smell out of it and let it air out a bit.  If you don't your ice will have a bad taste and smell to it.  Let a few cycles run through as well and dump out the ice.  You can fill it with your tap water or purified bottled water if you choose.  The ice will have a different texture and will be harder if you use the purified water.  I tried a gallon of "bought water" and it was clear and hard.  The water from my tap was white and soft.  I suppose it has something to do with the oxygen in the different types of water.  Nevertheless this is a good sized ice maker.  The ice dumps in the basket and keeps it cool pretty long.  Once it melts it just drops back into the water reservoir and is recycled back into making ice.

I originally purchased the Whirlpool replacement filters, but the cheaper alternatives were no longer available on Amazon. As these came in at a fraction of the cost and had somewhat good reviews I decided to give them a try. The filter, while it does work, is definitely different. First, the top part that slides into the handle is a lot smaller than the original, which means it slides around a lot. Not a deal breaker, but definitely different. Second, the twist connections on the tip are in a different location. Meaning, with the original filter I would put the filter in with the handle in the 12 o'clock position, then I would twist over to the arrow to the 3 o'clock position. With this one, I put it in with the handle at the 10 o'clock position, and stop at the 1 o'clock position. Again, not a deal breaker. Just annoying as it doesn't line up with the refrigerators built in arrows which would make one thing it's not screwed all the way in. Lastly, and this is the most annoying, is this filter is LOUD. I could always hear the water through the other filters when they were new before they were purged, but this one is consistently loud. So much so that I thought I didn't have it screwed in all the way. Going to go back to Whirlpool's filters, or look for a different alternative

I have learned a few things over the years.  First, I actually think the coffee tastes better if after brewing it there is a small layer around the edge of bubbly slurm. I noticed this when drinking coffee freshly brewed in cafes in Europe, there was always some bubbly or foamy stuff around the edges.  Second, I find I get a better cup of coffee with a coarse to very coarse grind.  Third, don't overfill the Gold K-up, that actually interferes with the filtration.  If anything, underfill slightly.  Fourth, if you don't want the residue in the bottom of the cup, pour it into another cup.  I don't find my Keurig heats my coffee well enough so I brew it into a good mug and then heat it up some more.  That allows me to pour most of it into my travel mug and leave the residue behind.  Surely if you like coffee made in a French Press you are used to the coffee residue that ends up in the bottom of  your coffee and that is supposed to be a superior method of making coffee.

The 16" width is long in comparison to others, but we sell corsets, dresses and other items which require a wider, 15" bag. It works just as well when sealing smaller width bags.

Because it has a metal housing, it has some "heft", and will not bounce around when quickly using it when sealing, and won't go flying across the table if you bump it. Overall, a nice product and a decent value.

Note: This will hermetically seal the bag completely, making it airtight. If you are selling apparel or similar items that might have a risk of damage from moisture, you might want to add a dessicant (i.e. a silica gel pack), to help absorb any moisture, if you are packing and sealing products in a humid environment. I use 1-gram silica gel packs, and you can find them on Amazon. The alternative is to punch a small hole in the corner of the sealed bag, so the item can "breathe," but then you risk warehouse dust making its way in.

https://www.amazon.com/Hermetic-Glass-Pitcher-Homemade-Bottles/dp/B0131EKHO0

and dilute with hot water whenever I want a cup (it's easy to adjust the strength to suit). The resulting cup is amazing. Highly recommended!
These bags are perfect for my needs and the quality is exactly as I hoped. This was my second purchase of these and the new loop size is much more to my liking. Highly recommended.

I've been using one of these bags to make cold brew coffee. It filters out about 99% of the sediment. I use the other one for racking my wine/mead must. It doesn't filter as well as the one for the coffee, but it works better than anything else I've tried, so I'm happy.

This filter bag does everything I could expect of it to make the process of cold brew coffee extremely easy. Negligible small sediment in the bottom of the pitcher. No holes and the elastic works well.

Perfect for making almond milk!  I love fresh, homemade almond milk but struggled to make it using cheese cloth (super messy & time consuming).  No more!  These bags make it so easy, fast and clean.  The cloth easily separates the milk from the gritty almond residue and leaves a super creamy & smooth milk.  Making almond milk now takes a few minutes with very little clean-up. Also, this size is perfect for making a 2 cup serving of almond milk (1 cup almonds & 2 cups water).  So happy to have discovered these!  Highly recommend!
Excellent product!  We use some classic old style Mason jars and steep the coffee for 1-2 days. Works perfectly and really keeps the grounds out of the liquid.

I just started making cold brew and was using cheesecloth/strainer method...until I found these wonderful bags! The cheesecloth was unbelievably messy and I always wound up with grounds and silt in my coffee no matter how careful I was. Even though I have arthritis, the elastic band is easy to use whether the bag is dry or wet. When squeezing the bag, the elastic band holds so well no grounds come out of the top and there is virtually no silt in my final coffee. The e-book was a great help too since I'm a newbie at this. Also, a shout out to this company--I contacted them with a question and they got back to me very quickly. Today I am attempting to make coconut milk using the other bag which I'm certain will work just as well. I'm looking forward to doing business with this company again in the future.
Love the bags! I've tried other options out there such as a metal/mesh strainers and these are way better!
little messy for cleaning out but over all like it
I haven't actually made cold brew coffee yet, although that's on the bucket list. Nut milk is our bag - and this is the perfect one for it! Thanks Organic Family Products!
These bags are really good.  Easy to use and the coffee tastes great!

Pretty fine mesh for cold brew coffee, keeping the finer grounds contained.  Obviously some escape and while I still paper filter the coffee before drinking, I can see some people not.  It is a little pricey for two cotton bags though.  Maybe next time I'll sew my own...or not.

Makes cold brew so easy. Elastic design is much superior to string ties.

Only issue I've had is a few threads coming loose at the bottom of the bag. I assume it'll eventually come loose, but it's still in good shape after 10+ batches. Haven't even used the second bag yet.
We are very happy with the bags. The cold brew is very good and easy to make!
I have used these to make cold brew coffee and cold brew tea. So far the product works amazingly well!

These bags work really well for smaller amounts. I have since started using them a secondary filter. I use a nylon mesh bag initially and then pour the cold brew into the bag whilst in a pitcher. It filters all the small particles very well. I will buy more when these wear out.
I just think they are pricey for what they are. I saw them cheaper at the store

I bought this cooler as an alternative to renting a cooler (which I did for years) from my water delivery service. I have been using it for almost a month and here's what I come away with.

Pros
1. It's a good looking piece of equipment and an attractive spot filler.
2. It offers a very nice HOT cup of water. I find myself using that function quite a bit. A very good thing about the 'hot' water button it has a
safety. It would be difficult for a child to accidentally be burned when dispensing or attempting to dispense water from either cold or hot side.
3. NO HEAVY LIFTING - it's bottom loaded, simple and very easy.
4. LED Indicator lights and alert sounds. When you're in need of replacement bottle it alerts you by sight and sound. Otherwise there is very little sound coming from the cooler, barely a hum. If it weren't for the lights I'd have to check to make sure it was still running. Lastly, the lights are a plus at night.

Cons
1. LED lights run all the time. There should be an option to turn them off.
2. As good as the hot water is at getting hot the cold water falls short. The water gets a chill not COLD. It gets just a little below room temp.
The cooler is placed at a diagonal position in a corner with 4" clearance on either side and 12" from the corner. That meets the requisite
requirements of placement to function optimally. I like really cold water and miss that from my previous

Works as described. Was disappointed that it sits so low and the opening between the base and the spout is really short so that larger bottles and pitchers don't fit. Overall it's a good product and I would recommend it.

Finding a reliable water dispenser turns out to be harder than it should be.  Keeping it clean so your family isn't getting sick from the bottled water is also a chore.  This is an excellent machine that works as advertised.  Cold water is cold; hot is hot.  The unit is sturdy and easy to use.  The self-cleaning feature is a god-send.  When the old Primo one that we had died (a little more ,than a year after we bought it), we did extensive research and settled on this Whirlpool.  It arrived many days earlier than the expected delivery date.  We are very satisfied.

So far, so good. I have only had it for a short while but it is, at least at this time a lot better than my old Primo top load model. It is very quiet. Even when the pump is sucking up the water from the bottle into the reservoir, it is quieter than the Primo one was when the compressor was running to cool the water. I can't barely hear the compressor on this on when it is running from across the room.

The best feature is that it is a bottom load so no more lifting bottles up top and less chance for an *accident*.

Well worth the extra money for this than buying a cheaper top load model. Plus it cleans it's self. The top load was annoying to clean every 6 months.
Nice!

Not sure if there is anything I have to do to make the water colder.  This is the main reason for docking one star.  Otherwise, this dispenser is quite good.

The Della spin drying washong machine is fantastic. It has a large impeller, 2 speeds, a stainless steel rinse/spin basket large enough to handle its washer tub capacity, as well as the conventional timers and funtion controls.

I bought mine on Ebay and it is the same machine. What I want to note is that the spin drier really removes excess water, This cuts drying time by about 35%. Finally it is a pristine beauty in white and turquoise.

Well, I saw the spinner timer didn't work when I tested the washer with the first small load. I thought I could deal with that. I'd just have to keep an eye on it. No problem. Then on the 4th load a few days later, the water pump stopped working. Both the spinner and the washer now have water in them. I'm not sure why the spinner does except maybe from the towel that I put into it. The spinner spins, but the water stays there, so nothing is going to get dry in it. I hoped this would be a solution for not having to go to the laundromat as often, but I seem to have gotten more problems than solutions.

UPDATE:
I contacted customer service and they were very professional and friendly. When I tried the washer again in order to send the seller a video to show the issues, the washer and dryer worked perfectly. The timer worked even though it had not worked at all since I got it. I'm not sure what happened. Maybe I didn't have the lids completely closed the first time? I don't know. lol But I'm updating this review, because everything is fine now and customer service was so great.

There are both pluses and minuses for the Panda.

I've been spoiled, I suppose, by the ease of the single-cup automatic coffee makers. But, they're not always eco-friendly. And, the coffee isn't always very fresh. Sometimes, I get gifts of coffee beans, or I just want to make a great cup of custom coffee, or I'm away from home with no maker in sight. Then, this paper-less pour-over coffee filter is perfect!

This pour-over coffee maker is perfect for the coffee afficionado who wants to have complete control over the temperature, grind, and mix of beans to water. The stainless steel is odorless and flavorless, so it won't interfere with the nuances of the coffee. If you're traveling, you don't need paper liners, either, so there's nothing else to bring with you, or worry about keeping dry. The mesh is so fine, there's no grounds in the bottom of my coffee cup, either!

Making a cup of coffee is as simple as heating some water, putting a scoop of grinds in the filter, wetting them, and then slowly pouring the rest of the water in. Following the technique for preparing pour over coffee, I wound up with a perfectly brewed and filtered cup of hot coffee and absolutely no fines or residue in the cup. I've had this ice machine for a few months now.  I'm an engineer, and I just love watching it make ice.  Purchase this unit with your eyes open, and you won't be disappointed.  When you open the machine, you'll notice a basket where the ice drops in after it's made.  Just below the basket is the water reservoir.  What this means is that this unit is not a freezer.  After the ice drops into the basket, you need to scoop it out and put it in a bag or whatever for your freezer - or use the ice as it's made.  After letting the ice refreeze in a freezer for ~30 minutes or so, break the ice up.  This will help prevent a solid ice brick forming.  I haven't had any problems with function as others have described, so I'm hopeful.  It doesn't take long for the first few ice cubes drop.  It's a lot faster than ice trays, and I don't want to have to go out and buy ice every time I run out. I've looked at quite a few units before settling on this one.  I traded some preferred functionality for cost, but overall I'm pleased with my purchase.

The walls of the water reservoir and water trough need to be cleaned of GUNK on a monthly basis of run 24/7 as I do run mine.
Most times all I clean it out w/ is paper towels held fast w/ a Hemostat. To get in between the refrigerating thingies that produce the ice.

Lint leads me to my first problem w/ this unit. Plugged up the water outlet that fills the water trough & caused the water to miss the trough by redirecting the water coming from the water outlet that fills the trough. I had to remove it's outer back panel & top in order to remove the lint blockage from the water outlet. The second problem is that the sensor that shuts down the unit when the basket is full has stopped doing it's thing. Minor problems that I or anyone else can overcome w/ a little resourcefulness. All in all, I say this icemaker is a very good buy. But that is up to the individual to ponder.

Now, after operating for a couple of weeks, I have a helpful hint. I was getting ice that was thicker at the top, of the unit, than bottom. The sheet of cubes didn't drop quite right. Every time I do I think of all of the current news stories involving dangerous or even poisonous tap water. I figured a filter, any filter, can only help. The fact that this comes with a pitcher and a filter that can be used with the pitcher or with almost anything else you have in the house was a bonus.

The pitcher is a serious disappointment to me. If were rating it alone, it'd get 1 star. The spout that closes for pouring has a gap in that allows water to pour out even when closed -- though it doesn't snap closed so if you bump the pitcher a little the spout flaps all around. The plastic feels cheap. It really need a different lid that doesn't pop off so easily. That's the bad.

The good is the filter itself is easy to use. It can be used in almost any pitcher or bottle you have at home. In fact If it's possible, I'd recommend buying the filter section without the pitcher. It has markings so you can see what month you starting using the filter. Although you CAN filter water fast, if you're not fond of wasting water I'd actually do it at a slower steady stream as the filter itself does not hold a lot of water so a lot of water is literally going down the drain as it pours out over the filter. 2) It is very attractive and modern looking. Because of the appearance it looks really clean. The packaging it came in was also very modern and clean appearing,
3) It fills faster than any other water treatment system that I am aware of.
Filters right from your tap water.
Editorial comment---I think slicing some fresh fruit and adding it to the pitcher would make it even more appealing.
Very nice item---so glad to call it mine.

This is a nice looking filter pitcher, however, it takes up a lot more space on my fridge shelf than the narrow Brita pitcher I have. The only way to let this fill directly from the faucet is with a very thin stream of water. I have always just filled the reservoir of the Brita, then put it in the fridge to drip down. This one requires watching. I did a "taste test" of this pitcher and the Brita and found no difference. It looks like the replacement filters for this are pretty pricey, and not sure of how available. Perhaps the funnel that can be used in other containers makes it worthwhile. It is attractive, nice design.

The pros: it removes chlorine smell and taste from our city water. The pitcher is attractive for serving use. The pour spout rocks - it has a little self-opening flip-top cover, and it pours quickly without dripping. That, and the cover for the filtration section, would help keep insects out if using this outdoors.

The cons: it would be nice to have some kind of marks indicating cups on the pitcher, for filling our teakettle with an appropriate amount of water for our teapots. The filtration is rather slow, but not more so than other similar devices; however, because of the size of the filtration space, one must keep the unit under the faucet for an extended period of time. It's a tall pitcher, so if you have a low faucet, this could be an issue. I would not want to hold the filtration device in my hand to fill another container because it would be so time-consuming. I used to own a Britta and one could fill the top reservoir and then set the pitcher down, and the filtration part would just work at it's own speed. This is an interesting idea. It spreads out the filter like a drip coffee maker. This larger area makes the water pass through faster. It would be impossible for it to pass as slowly as my leading brand, and some people are saying it is slower, which based on physics is impossible.

This filter unfortunately does not seem to perform as advertised. While there is a lot to like about it, it only offers trade-offs over current filters on the market. Ultimately it's more of a hassle over traditional filters.

Setup and activation of the filter is a process. There are a number of components that need to be washed and assembled. The filter needs to be soaked for some time, and due to the fact that the filter tends to float, I spent the time to hold it under the water to ensure a complete activation. It never actually stayed submerged during this process. The final step is shaking the filter.

Once assembled, it performed nicely for a few days. I could leave the pitcher in the sink to fill up under a moderate stream and it would only take a minute or so. The performance quickly dropped, however. Now it takes a few minutes to fill up under only a trickle. Any faster and the reservoir on top overflows and leaks into the filtered water. It seems like a step backward.

The other filters on the market that have a more thorough filter and a larger reservoir actually perform better. You can fill up your water bottle from the pitcher, then fill up the pitcher reservoir walk away. With this, you have to stand there waiting for it to fill. It's a step backward. And the fact that the filter on this product is only a fraction of the filtering capability of others doesn't really help.

This is a scam as several other reviewers noticed. First, the "Blue Signature" water filter claims a NSF testing for both NSF 42 & 53. Looking up the NSF database shows no product certification for "Blue Signature". You can check it on the info-nfs-org website.

I find it convenient to use two 5-gallon plastic buckets for water drainage, alternating them when they're about half full. When the first bucket is about half full, I turn off the Drain setting. When the water pauses its flow through the hose, I slip the hose into the next bucket and flip the dial back to the Drain setting while emptying the first bucket. It's quite easy to lift half a bucket of water and empty it into the toilet or tub, and I can repeat the procedure with alternating buckets as long as I need to.
There is a lint filter in the washer section, and it's worth checking/cleaning out once a month or so, depending upon your volume of weekly wash.

•And it doesn't take much water or time!

Cons:
•The dryer portion is tiny (so you can't put much in there)

•The spin portion of the washer barely moved the clothes (so if you have pets this will not remove the hair from clothes)
•The water hose doesn't actually hook up the the sink (I just use a 5 gallon bucket to fill it and drain into)

He purchased a hanging clothes rack that he'll sit outside to dry. The unit fits perfectly inside his walk-in shower and does not connect it a facet. Instead, he uses the shower head to fill the unit as needed. It is noisy and it sometimes doesn't drain when it in that setting. But he's discovered that unplugging the unit for a few seconds and turning the wash to drain mode, easily fixes the problem. The spin bin is small and will require the clothes be spun in 2 batches. It does not dry the clothes. It only wrings them out to about 90% dry, depending on the fabric.

Just remember to keep the doors open otherwise the washer will start to have a mildew smell. He uses this washer 99% of the time instead of using the commercial coin washer in his building. I recommended using a scent booster such as Gain so his clothes always have a nice scent to them.

First let me mention the function of this is not fully automatic. You have to add your clothes, then add your water. I used a very small amount of laundry detergent. Set it for 15 minutes and it did agitation cycles for 15 minutes. Then you have to select drain and drain all the water. Next you have to refill the tub with fresh water to do the rinse. Set it for another 15 minutes, then drain that water. Then you can transfer your laundry to the spin dryer. The spin dryer is essentially just the spin cycle on a larger washing machine. So, this is NOT REALLY a dryer, just a spin cycle. Your clothes will be close to dry and can be hung or, as I chose to do, get a warm air drying rack. I got a decent one for $84 that has hangers and a cloth housing that directs all the warm air through the laundry.

Bottom line is that this unit is great and does its job, but still requires your involvement and time. You can't just throw laundry in and come back to clean laundry. On a positive note, I have exceptional control on how the cycles work and how many times I want to rinse my clothes and how exact I want my water temp, etc. This unit can manage for 1 person, not a family.

A few details: I live in NYC on a third floor walkup in a tiny 500 sq ft apartment.

PROS:

- Its FAST but requires some work: The way it works is you fill up the laundry, add water/detergent and set the wash for 15 mins. After that, you flip a switch, and the panda automatically drains itself. You refill, and run a rinse cycle (also 15 mins). - It's basically a giant, sturdy piece of plastic. I'm borderline emotional about it, but it is absolutely high quality, and very much designed to be simple and with the end user in mind.
- For what it does, it's surprisingly quiet (unless you load the spinner wrong - see cons).

Once the plunger is securely screwed into the bottom plate, the screen will stay centered and coffee grounds will not seem around the oversized hole.  The edge of the screen is trimmed more neatly than the original screen that came with the coffee press, but it still could be done better. I was excited to see that I can now purchase MUCH less expensive compatible water filters for my LG refrigerator rather than the ridiculously priced LG water filters.  When we purchased our new LG refrigerator we bought the extended warranty mainly because by doing so we would get a 30% rebate on the water filters every 6 months over the course of the warranty which the savings would in turn pay for the warranty.  The regular price for the LG water filter for our refrigerator is $49.98 and with the warranty we can get a $15 rebate bringing the cost of the filter down to $35.  If we purchased a filter every six months as suggested by the manufacturer during the 5 year warranty the savings would be equal to what the warranty cost ($150).  Sounded like a win/win -- coverage for the refrigerator and the savings on the water filters would pay for the warranty.  However, we have had our refrigerator almost two years now and have only purchased 2 water filters (we just don't use that much filtered water/ice).  In fact, when we have replaced the filter, it didn't really need to be replaced.  The water still tasted good and the ice was still crystal clear.  We only did so because 6 months had passed.  Anyway, you have to call and request a rebate submission authorization and after sending them the documentation it takes about 2 1/2 months to get the $15 rebate check.  Ended up being a lot of trouble for $15 in my opinion.  Since these filters are under $20, they work every bit as well

The mesh filter is just big enough to let the coffee seep and fine enough to not let sediment through. Some oil can get through but produces a bigger, bolder cup than paper filters with no sediment.

I use a grind between french press and pour over to control the water flow for both hot and iced coffee. You can grind finer for a bigger bodied cup or coarser for a cleaner cup. Either way this filter performs and is easy to clean. Just experiment to find your grind size because this filter will perform based on that.

Dont waste time and money on other filters when this one hits the mark.

Anyway, this design is very well made, but actually has two layers (screen and perforated metal sheet). It also has a flat spot in the bottom. My theory is that the Able Kone, which does not have the two-layer design or flat spot, has better water-flow through the coffee. This prevents bitterness, I believe. Note that I have been using metal filters for years, and tested this design a couple of weeks. I tried adjusting my grind and changing my pouring technique. Nothing stopped the bitterness.

In case anyone is doubting my technique, here it is:

70 grams of quality beans, ground medium on a Virtuoso burr grinder, Able Kone filter with Chemex glass carafe. Water boiled and then poured into a cool stainless pouring carafe. Wet, the grounds, wait a minute, and then pour slow and steady over the grounds. This creates a strong brew that gets rave reviews.

(And no, I don't work for Able or any other coffee-related company. I'm just a coffee dependent guy looking out for my fellow jittery Johns and Janes.)

So all the reviews I read about this machine were accurate. You need to put a little work into it for it to be just perfect.
What you will need:
Garden Hose
Hose connecting Adapter
Clamp Rings
Eye Hoods
Craft Wire

Working with what you have:
The hose is 2 small and you need an adapter. I found a simple solution by going to home depot and getting a clear hose to attach to the hose. Before inserting the hose I inserted a plastic connector into the open end of the washing machine hose.
This allowed the hose to remain in place in the clear hose.
I then used clamp rings to make sure it would not come out and hold it together.
I have made this portable mini washing machine into a non-movable one by putting the hose to drain in the sink.
I attached eye hooks to the wall and used craft wire to wrap around the hose and threaded it through the hooks.
The hose for intake is also too small.
Easy fix for that situation as well.
I took a garden hose found an adapter for my kitchen sink ( don't drink tap water anyway so removed tap filter to place adapter)
Now when I want to use the machine I only have to connect the hose and fill the tub with hot or cold water depending on what I'm washing.

So the device did meet its accuracy specification. I expected too much for the price. As an electrical engineer that spent a career designing measurement instruments, I should have recalled that a temperature sensor alone with a measurement accuracy specification better than +/- 5 degrees F would cost more than I paid for this meter.. That's why more accurate meters are calibrated for accuracy and cost more because of the labor cost of calibration. You get what you pay for, and at ten dollars this device meets specifications at a modest price. Hence four stars. Good device for the money if you can accept temperature accuracy of +/- 2 degrees. Lightweight, easy to move around. It washes well and the spinner is very powerful.
My suggestions are: do not put too much soap, it is not necessary . After your first wash, drain the water, and then fill the machine with water only again and let it run for a minute, and then drain again. That should help you get rid of the soap. If not, that means that you either put too much soap or you load is a bit big. In that case, just rinse it again. I do not run water while the spinner is active. I simply rinse my clothes twice in clean water in the same section where I washed them. At the second rinse I add softener. Then I drain the water and transfer clothes to the spinner. That's it. When it comes to items that are made of thin fabric, or are sensitive, even including men's dress shirts, always spin for two minutes first. Then take the items out to see if they are dry enough. If you let them spin too long, it might be a bit aggressive for the fabric. For towels I do five minutes.
Make sure that you clean the lint collector regularly. My only problem with the machine is that by time it started to fail to drain properly. Looks like the pump is not good anymore.
Do not overload the spinner. Just be patient and try to wash your laundry every other day, so it would not pile-up . That way you will not complain how your machine cannot wash a big load at once. :-)

So I have been using the gentle cycle and have received great results.

Since this isn't an actual dryer, I also include 1/4 cup white vinegar when washing with the detergent and the fabric softener to keep the clothes soft. Here's my process:

1. Fill washer with water, clothes, detergent, and vinegar. Run for 15 minutes.
2. Drain & refill washer with water. Add fabric softener & 1/4 white vinegar. Run 15 minutes.
3. Place half the load in the dryer/spinner. I run water for 3 minutes while it spins in the spinner (for a final rinse), then reset for 5 minutes to let clothes dry.
4. Clothes are mostly dry and I hang them.

For those of you who are questioning the smell of vinegar, it dissipates : )

Hope this helps! Enjoy

This coffee maker relies on a slow drip, about 4-5 minutes. I heat water up to boiling point. Then grind the beans at a medium grind , put base filter in pot, pour coffee over this filter and try to get the grinds level in the pot. A small tamper would work here. I am still working on this. Then screw the top filter on to stem of bottom filter. But not too tight or water may not get through. Try screwing down the top filter just enough to touch the grounds. Then pour in at least one cup of hot water. Back up: The pot needs to sit on top  of  coffee mug or glass, then pour water over it. Cover while dripping to save flavor. You can add milk before or after water is added, if you use it. This procedures is WELL worth the wait, because the flavor does not have the sharp bite that high pressure espresso machines can create. The result is strong but mellow! And that IS incredible!  Ed

Updating - I bought a Della last year (March 2016) So we've not quite had it a year. We hit a series of problems listed in the order below and btw I've noticed other people complain of similar things happening

1) the add water light comes on when there is a full reservoir - this is likely caused by lint or something stopping up the tubing. Also there is a little motor that brings the water up from the reservoir to the icemaker, we had a tiny hair wrapped around the gear.

Also 2) it will overheat - solution is to brush the dust off the compressor coils.

3) it got out of sync - and keeps going backward and forward never actually stopping to make ice - in ours there are 2 switchs that must be "hit" to cycle through the ice making process. Those switches each have a spring inside and we guess the spring is either broken or came off, at this point it is likely not worth fixing.

We've gone through all of this with our Della, as I said we are now at problem #3. My husband is a whiz at fixing things so we literally wear things out before replacing. I would love to be able to fix it but we do not know who to call to order parts - this is where warranties come in. Wish we'd had one. I am now researching ice makers to replace the Della

The item delivered to me is not the same as what is shown on the Amazon site.

See my photos. The original OEM Kenmore filter is at the top of each photo; replacement air filter from Amazon on bottom.

While the replacement filter does fit properly in my Kenmore refrigerator, the materials and construction are decidedly different than the OEM filter that came with the refrigerator. The original OEM Kenmore filter is constructed with the black, perforated (punched holes) carbon filter sandwiched between two sheets of white fabric filter material. The air filter replacement delivered from Amazon (from LG?) is made of a black "honeycomb" material (tiny holes) and lacked the two sheets of fabric filter material. However, the replacement does appear to have a black fabric material laminated to one side of the carbon filter.

Is the replacement a fair replacement or improved design? We'll see. I'm not a fan of inaccurate/false advertising, so 2 stars until the item supplied matches what they are advertising.

I purchased the Simple cup reusable K-cups last year for my then-new K-50 coffee maker.

I now use them with some caution. I still like the system.

Don't overfill,or overpack (i.e. tamp) these cups. The Keurig is not an espresso maker.

When you fill them, use a teaspoon or small spoon to loosely load the coffee in the container and filter, before pushing the cap on the unit. If there are some extra dry grounds on the cap afterwards, either shake the excess coffee back in your coffee supply, or discard the remainder. You don't want the extra grounds on the cap surface.

I learned my lesson after having coffee grounds clog the machine. I was tired, got sloppy and stuffed the cup and filter with too much coffee. Then, I couldn't get the Keurig to brew properly. My award for my impatience was the receipt of a weak cup of lukewarm amber water with some coffee grounds in it. It looked more like the tap water in my old apartment.

Fortunately, and with some patience, I was able remedy the problem by using a paper clip to unclog the three nozzle assembly, and flush the reservoir to resolve the problem. My next step was to use vinegar on the initial flush, and enough water to flush the vinegar smell out of the unit afterwards. If you use these filters exclusively, consider brewing a cup of hot water weekly (no K-Kup or Simple Cup inserted in machine) through the system to prevent clog problems.

A weaker or stronger brew is easy to accomplish by simply adjusting the amount of grounds used.

There are some loose ends that in my opinion need to be addressed. Those things to correct are the following:

1. When you use the timer, the led of timer goes off when returns to Temp or Power instead of remaining it on, so you have the information that the timer is activated together with the function light of Power or Temp;
2. 10 levels of temperature is just too little, jumping 20 degrees is to much to allow better tuning, 10 degrees is the maximum acceptable;
3. Heating by temperature setting always assumes maximum power, something that might burn the ingredients, like milk. The temperature adjustment should assume the power defined previously before switching, to be able to achieve a temperature through a preferred power.

To solve all the previous points, it will be more intuitive if the functions were cumulative, Power and Temperature and/or Time. Given a Power, it should be possible to restrict by Temperature and Timer, where the value 0 means no restriction, and so, no light informing the existing restriction! The Power light means it's on while the others ones mean the respective restriction, temperature and time function, ideally with an unitary adjustment in degrees and minutes. I bought this to test out what induction cooking is like as we were considering buying an in-counter cooktop. I love the idea of induction cooking—I remember as a kid (when induction was crazy expensive) I thought it was so Star Trek that I could barely wait the 30 years it would take for me to be in a position to buy a stovetop. And better yet, it doesn't produce the excess heat waste that any other power source does, so it is greener *and* more pleasant to use. (Gas and electric pump waste heat out pretty bad, and to double the inefficiency, that generally means you air conditioner will be doing extra duty.)

The promise of precision cooking and near-immediate temperature changes is really exciting, but this model absolutely doesn't live up. I've tested with laser thermometers and plain boil tests in a variety of good pans, and this one has bad hot-spots and cold spots; adjusting the temperature doesn't take effect quickly, even if you change it by a lot; and anything above 3 or 4 (on a scale of TEN) is way too hot for most anything except nuking a pot of water.

I DO UNDERSTAND that an inexpensive tabletop model could never be a very accurate example of what cooking on a "real" Bertazzoni or Wolf or GE cooktop or range would be like. Nevertheless, I was hoping this would be good enough to give us the confidence of buying an expensive induction cooktop, and it did the opposite.

The Delibru reusable cups for Keurig brewers have a "shower head" design and lots of screen area, including the bottom. In fact, there's so much screen, and so little plastic frame, that it feels flimsy. The bottom screen is recessed to prevent it from being punctured by the Keurig's bottom piercing needle (good) but that method of protecting it also reduces the volume for coffee, thereby limiting brew strength significantly. Because the side screen extends almost to the lid, a portion of the incoming water bypasses most of the coffee grounds, further weakening the brew. I tried various grinds (including fine) trying to find the sweet spot. But I was never able to make decent coffee except at the Keurig's smallest cup size.

I stopped using these and tried a competing product by ValueCafe (6-pack for $7.99 on Amazon), which is apparently a very new design. It's very sturdy, has a protected bottom screen. a real hinge for the lid, and is also a "shower head" design. I was very pleased with the ValueCafe product (see review)). It's so new the picture on the box did not correspond to the product (but the web page pictures did) and there were no instructions on the box or enclosed with the product. Hopefully, ValueCafe will fix those issues quickly.

Where the ice is made is freezing (obviously), but the storage area is just insulated.
When the ice basket is full, the machine goes to sleep.

Running, the unit draws 108W (as measured with a "Kill-A-Watt" meter)
Over a 10 day test period, my unit consumed 6.34 kWh. That's 0.63 kWh per day (11 cents worth of power where I live).
My family (4 adults) uses ice in everything. A drink of water typically starts with a glass full of ice.

Works like a champ, but I recommend these procedures and considerations. If you expect to unpack the Igloo 103 and in 10 minutes have enough ice for a party, this ain't for you.
First, unpack, place on the level surface on which the little guy will do his stuff, and let it set until tomorrow (next day). The manual says let it set 10 hours.
Second (next day), after you untape the ice bucket and scoop, rinse them with hot water then dry. Also, wipe out the interior with a damp multi layer paper towel.
Third, fill a gallon jug with filtered water and pour into the water chamber to just below the max fill line (won't use the entire gallon).
Fourth, install the ice bucket and close the lid.
Fifth, plug in and let it go to work.
When you press start, the machine defaults to medium size ice cubes. I recommend you leave it at this setting until you've let the machine run for about three (3) hours. You may discover "medium" is the perfect size.
On the first operation, expect the first ice in about 20 minutes. Don't expect the first few ice drops to be useful. The ice maker will start dropping cubes about every 10 minutes or so. It takes about two hours to get the ice to the correct size and have enough to fill a large glass. At three hours, you'll have enough ice for, maybe, three large glasses or four or five smaller glasses. This gadget is strictly for family use and small gatherings. You can place single serve brewers into two basic categories, those that preheat water (ex. Keurig 55 and larger) and those that don't (ex. Keurig 15). Those that preheat water have a water storage reservoir and a hidden, internal tank that keeps a quantity of water hot all the time the unit is powered on so that multiple cups can be made quickly. Those that don't preheat water have to be filled up with water for each cup, EXCEPT for a few models like the Cuisinart SS-5 that have a water storage reservoir, but no preheating tank.  With a Keurig 55 you wait for about 4 minutes of preheating to get that first cup to start filling after turning the machine on, then you waste electricity by keeping water hot until the unit goes into power saving mode or you turn it off. With the Cuisinart SS-5 you wait about 20 seconds for each cup to start filling and it makes a hot cup, hotter than the single-serve Keurig 15, and without having to refill the reservoir for every cup or keep internal water hot that may never be used that day. I think that Cuisinart solves the problem of under-heated water by dispensing water more slowly than Keurig units and only running a pump at the end, rather than running a pump the whole time like Keurig does, so it takes a little longer but you still get a very hot cup. I have used it for awhile now with no problems, and it really is a good solution for some of us. It is compact and stylish and better designed than some Keurig models that hog space and look

I thought I was going to be blown away and love this coffeemaker, but so far I only really, really like it. I read the reviews, I watched the videos comparing it to the Keurig and to the older model Cuisinart, my expectations were really high. The main thing keeping me from loving it is that it's slightly slower than my old Keurig.

Here are the things that I really, really like about it:
- The water is noticeably hotter than my old Keurig, so the coffee tastes better, stronger.
- It looks much sleeker and takes up a bit less room on my counter. The reservoir isn't lit, so it's more low-key.
- It holds a bit more water in the reservoir and it doesn't need to be filled as quickly.
- It's ready to brew the instant you turn it on.

Here are the things that keep me from loving it:
- It's slower than my old Keurig Platinum...not much slower, but it is slower.
- It doesn't really need a hot water button, since it does the same thing as the brew button...you still need to remove the pod.
- The handle to open the head feels flimsy, I worry that it'll break quickly.

So, overall, I really, really like it. I could love it if only it was a little faster. And the temperature is absolute perfection, so that part alone made me keep it.

This filter definitely took a few frustrating times to get the hang of, but taking into account the laws of hydrodynamics, I realized that "burping" the correct way is a crucial step. You need to pre-fill with enough water before adding grounds so that you can remove the rubber stopper and release some of the pre-brewed water to prep/"burp" the filter in the correct direction before adding grounds. Then, after brewing, when you're ready to release the coffee, the filter has been sitting in the correct orientation and the coffee will flow freely through the filter. Not disturbing the grounds after adding them also helps, otherwise they will tend to get sucked towards the filter with the escaping coffee and block the filter holes.

This is exactly what we were looking for. We use it not only for beverages, but also as an overflow refrigerator. The shelves are removable, which allows you to store larger items when needed (such as a gallon of milk).

We keep the unit in the "mud room", where the ambient temperature is a fairly steady 60 degrees in the Winter (will be closer to 80 degrees in the Summer). I like my drinks cold, so I put it on the "5" setting (two notches below the coldest setting). This keeps it right near 32 degrees. Any colder and the drinks would freeze. I expect that I will need to set it to "7" in the Summer.

Overall, it does the job at the right price; looks nice; and is not a loud unit. The only drawback is that the internal light is manual, not automatic. If you operate the unit in a dark place, I could see it possibly being a slight inconvenience to have to manually the switch the light on and off each time. But in my case, this is not a problem. It is also still too early to tell how much impact this will have on my electric bill.

I could tell these filters were perhaps not as effective as the OE filters - the flow rate was very high, suggesting to me that the water was moving through the carbon awfully quick (therefore maybe not as much carbon?). The first filter lasted a very long time, which struck me as odd, as I thought it should bugger up after awhile. Anyway, the real trouble started after I replaced the first filter. The morning after I changed the filter, I can to my kitchen to find my refrigerator and floor flooded. The filter was not seating properly. Removing and reinstalling the filter did not correct the problem. So I tossed the second filter and went for a third. Same issue - it leaked all over the fridge and floor. There were no visible defects or issues, but the filter was not seating and locking properly.

At this point, I said screw it and paid the full price for a Samsung OE filter. Worked perfectly and without issue.
